title: The trianguline variety and its local model
summary: This roadmap compares generic trianguline deformation spaces with completed double-flag incidence varieties, retaining character weights and both framings. It derives local normality, tangent bounds, companion criteria and local cycle identities, then develops the crystabelline deformation and higher-intertwining parameters used to recover Hodge filtrations. A separate local branch supplies the ordered-regular tangent and numerical noncriticality inputs to eigenvariety arguments.
readme:
This roadmap compares generic trianguline deformation spaces with completed double-flag incidence varieties, retaining character weights and both framings. It derives local normality, tangent bounds, companion criteria and local cycle identities, then develops the crystabelline deformation and higher-intertwining parameters used to recover Hodge filtrations. A separate local branch supplies the ordered-regular tangent and numerical noncriticality inputs to eigenvariety arguments.

The thirteen layers follow the construction order of the local-model proof and a separate ordered-regular local branch. The detailed reader fixes coefficient categories, sign conventions, both framings, source corrections and supplier contracts. The general locally analytic multiplicity assertion is explicitly conjectural. This is a complete target-level plan, not a formalisation; Artinian period and locally analytic constituent suppliers still need the extensions recorded in its packet.

stages.title: Framed almost de Rham deformation adapters
stages.description:
Almost de Rham deformation groupoids. For an almost de Rham E⊗B_dR representation W of rank n, X_W(A) is the groupoid of pairs (W_A,ι:W_A⊗_A E≅W), with equivariant isomorphisms compatible with ι. X_W^pdR adds an A⊗K-linear frame α_A:(A⊗K)^n≅D_pdR(W_A) lifting a fixed α. Pullback along A→B is tensor product, retaining the special-fibre identification.

The framed matrix deformation model. X_W^pdR is equivalent to the discrete deformation functor represented by the completion of g=Res_{K/Q_p} gl_n,E at N=α⁻¹ν_Wα. The forgetful map X_W^pdR→X_W is formally smooth of relative dimension dn². The target is the full Lie algebra completion, including infinitesimal matrices whose characteristic polynomial is not X^n.

Filtered period deformations and their weights. For a full G_K-stable B_dR flag F_• of W with rank-one graded pieces, define X_{W,F}(A) using a lifted full flag in W_A and its reduction to F_•; add α_A for X^pdR_{W,F}. Let κ_F be the ordered scalars by which ν acts on the graded A⊗K lines. Thus κ_F lies in m_A⊗_Qp K^n and is independent of α_A.

The first simultaneous-resolution model. The frame and D_pdR identify X^pdR_{W,F} with the completion of g̃ at (α⁻¹D_pdR(F_•),N); under this identification κ_F is the Cartan projection of the simultaneous resolution. This framed functor is formally smooth of dimension dn².

stages.title: Regular period lattices and Hodge flags
stages.description:
The period-lattice filtration adapter. For an almost de Rham lattice W⁺⊂W, send it to the decreasing filtration Fil^i D_pdR(W)=(t^i B_pdR⁺⊗_{B_dR⁺}W⁺)^{G_K}. This is exhaustive, separated and ν-stable. Conversely recover W⁺ as the ν=0 horizontal part of Σ_i t^(−i) B_pdR⁺⊗_K Fil^i. These constructions are inverse and compatible with morphisms.

Artinian lattice and filtration equivalence. The preceding equivalence extends over A∈Art_E to finite free A⊗B_dR⁺ representations and finite free A⊗K modules with nilpotent ν and exhaustive separated ν-stable filtrations whose graded pieces are finite projective over A⊗K. Filtration, graded pieces and the equivalence commute with tensoring any finite A-module. At each τ every graded piece is A-free, but ranks may be zero and need not be parallel in τ.

Regular lattices and the Hodge flag. A lattice is regular when its Sen weights are distinct at every τ. For their increasing ordering h_{τ,i}, form the increasing full flag Fil_i=⊕_τ Fil^(−h_{τ,i})_τ D_pdR(W). In every Artinian deformation the ranks of all graded τ-pieces equal the residual ranks, so the same indexed jumps define a lifted full flag.

The second simultaneous-resolution model. For a regular W⁺, its D_pdR-framed lattice deformation groupoid is equivalent to the completion of g̃ at (HodgeFlag(W⁺),N). It is formally smooth of dimension dn². The Cartan coordinates are the ν-scalars on the Hodge graded lines.

stages.title: Localized triangulations and character weights
stages.description:
Generic ordered parameter tuples. Let T be the rigid space of continuous characters K×→E×. Define T₀ⁿ by requiring, for every ordered i≠j, both δ_i/δ_j and εδ_j/δ_i to be nonalgebraic, where ε=N_{K/Qp}|N_{K/Qp}|. Define T_regⁿ by excluding δ_i/δ_j=∏ττ^(−aτ) and δ_i/δ_j=ε∏ττ^aτ for all aτ≥0 and every i≠j. The first condition is stronger than the regular rank-one cohomology condition; these loci must not be confused with NT regularity.

Localized triangulations and deformation parameters. For M=D[1/t], a localized triangulation F_• is an exhaustive full flag by finite projective (φ,Γ)-submodules with graded pieces R_E[1/t](δ_i). Define X_{M,F} by lifting this flag and M over Art_E. Its parameter map ω sends a lift to the unique tuple δ_A reducing to the specified residual tuple δ whose localized rank-one modules identify with its graded pieces. Without fixing δ, the tuple is only determined up to algebraic twists.

Rank-one torsion and localized isomorphisms. For k=(kτ)≥0 and a continuous δ:K×→E×, H⁰ and H¹ of R_E(δ)/(∏τtτ^kτ) vanish if every wtτ(δ) avoids {1−kτ,…,0}; by dévissage the same holds over A∈Art_E when the residual character satisfies this condition. If every labelled weight of a field-valued δ belongs to its indicated interval, both have E-dimension d. An isomorphism R_A[1/t](δ)≅R_A[1/t](δ′) exists exactly when δ/δ′ is an algebraic character with fixed integral exponents; this includes nilpotent coefficient information.

Localized period realization over Artinian coefficients. The B-pair functor gives an exact, coefficient-base-change-compatible W_dR from (φ,Γ)-modules M over R_{A,K}[1/t] to finite free A⊗B_dR representations of rank rk M. Here M is finite free over R_{A,K}[1/t] and contains a φ,Γ-stable R_K-lattice, which need not be free over R_{A,K}; W_dR(M) is independent of that lattice. For a (φ,Γ)-module D over R_{A,K}, W_dR⁺(D) is finite free of rank rk D and commutes with tensoring finite A-modules. On localized triangulations W_dR sends the full flag to a G_K-stable full flag.

Character weights equal period Cartan coordinates. For a residual field-valued rank-one character δ, W_dR(R_E[1/t](δ)) is almost de Rham if and only if δ is locally algebraic. For an Artinian deformation δ_A of such a δ, ν on D_pdR(W_dR(R_A[1/t](δ_A))) is multiplication by wt(δ_A)−wt(δ). Hence for a localized flag κ_F=wt(ω)−wt(δ), embedding by embedding. The rank-one period representation is trivial precisely when δ_A is locally algebraic, including the absence of infinitesimal weight variation.

stages.title: Extension comparison and formal lifting
stages.description:
The localized Herr-to-period extension map. Exact period realization induces a natural map H¹_{φ,Γ}(M)→H¹(G_K,W_dR(M)) by sending an extension of R_A[1/t] by M to its period extension. For almost de Rham W, H⁰(G_K,W)=ker ν and H¹(G_K,W)=coker ν on D_pdR(W); in particular H¹ is right exact, and is exact on the subcategory ν=0.

Rank-one localization and period comparison. If δ and εδ⁻¹ are nonalgebraic, H⁰(t^(−k)R_E(δ))=H²(R_E(δ))=0. The H¹ localization map is an isomorphism when wtτδ avoids {1,…,kτ} for every τ, and is zero when every wtτδ lies in that interval. If δ is additionally locally algebraic, H¹(R_E[1/t](δ))→H¹(G_K,W_dR(R_E[1/t](δ))) is an isomorphism. Over A with generic residual δ, localized H⁰ and H² vanish; the H¹ map is surjective if residual δ is locally algebraic and an isomorphism if δ_A itself is locally algebraic.

Formal smoothness of the filtered period comparison. For M with a localized triangulation of locally algebraic generic residual parameter δ, the map X_{M,F}→T̂_δⁿ×_{t̂₀}X_{W_dR(M),F} is formally smooth. Its points retain both the lifted character tuple and the lifted period flag with matching κ. This assertion holds for groupoids and all small extensions in Art_E.

Closed triangulation condition and split de Rham lifts. For a generic residual localized triangulation, X_{M,F}→X_M is relatively representable by a closed immersion. If the residual δ is locally algebraic generic and an Artinian deformation M_A has ν_{W_dR(M_A)}=0, then M_A splits as ⊕_i R_A[1/t](δ_{A,i}) with locally algebraic lifted parameters. The splitting assertion is not asserted without ν=0.

stages.title: The double-flag model and Galois components
stages.description:
Robba deformation gluing through the period lattice. For D with M=D[1/t], W⁺=W_dR⁺(D) and W=W_dR(M), deformation groupoids satisfy X_D≃X_M×_{X_W}X_{W⁺}. With a fixed localized flag, X_{D,F}≃X_{M,F}×_{X_W}X_{W⁺}; the same identities hold with compatible D_pdR frames. The flag on D is required only after inverting t, not integrally.

Representability of the comparison morphisms. Assume the localized triangulation has a parameter in T₀ⁿ. The morphisms X_M→X_W, X_{M,F}→X_{W,F}, X_D→X_{W⁺}, and X_{D,F}→X_{W⁺,F} are relatively prorepresentable; the last two are base changes of the first two. They satisfy the relative Schlessinger fibre-product criterion and have finite-dimensional relative tangent spaces. The character-weight map T̂_δⁿ→t̂₀ is formally smooth of relative dimension n.

Framed localized deformation dimension. For locally algebraic generic δ, X^pdR_{M,F} is prorepresented by a formally smooth complete local E-algebra of dimension d(n²+n(n+1)/2). Adding fixed rank-one graded bases instead gives a smooth rigidified functor of dimension n+dn(n+1)/2; forgetting those bases has relative dimension n. The n graded rescalings must not be counted as dn.

The double-flag formal local model. Assume δ locally algebraic generic and W⁺ regular. Set x_pdR=(α⁻¹D_pdR(F_•),α⁻¹HodgeFlag(W⁺),N) in X=g̃×_g g̃. The functor X^pdR_{W⁺,F} is represented by X̂_{x_pdR}; X^pdR_{D,F}→X̂_{x_pdR} is formally smooth of relative dimension dn(n+1)/2. Its completed local ring is a formal power-series algebra of that relative dimension over the completed incidence local ring.

Component deformation conditions. For w∈(S_n)^Σ define X^{pdR,w}_{D,F}=X^pdR_{D,F}×_{X̂}X̂_w and similarly for the lattice–flag functor. Let S(x_pdR)={w:x_pdR∈X_w}. Descend the condition after forgetting α; G-equivariance of X_w makes the unframed condition independent of α. Empty components are retained as empty functors, not zero rings declared to be domains.

Normality of the framed component rings. For w∈S(x_pdR), X^{pdR,w}_{D,F} is represented by a complete local normal domain of dimension d(n²+n(n+1)/2), formally smooth over X̂_{w,x_pdR} with relative dimension dn(n+1)/2. Cohen–Macaulayness follows from the imported local-model CM theorem and formal smoothness; neither conclusion asserts smoothness of X_w.

Weight-graph detection of a component. Let Θ=(κ_triangulation,κ_Hodge):X_{D,F}→(t×_{t/S}t)^∧_(0,0). For w∈S(x_pdR), its restriction to X^w_{D,F} factors through the completed graph T_{w′}={(z,(w′)⁻¹z)} if and only if w′=w; the framed version is equivalent. This is scheme-theoretic factorization, including nilpotent Artinian weight directions.

Framed Galois component rings. Let r:G_K→GL_n(E) have D=D_r and a generic locally algebraic localized triangulation, with regular W⁺. The framed Galois functor X_{r,F} is prorepresented by a reduced equidimensional complete local ring R_{r,F} of dimension n²+dn(n+1)/2. Its minimal primes p_w are indexed by S(x_pdR); R_{r,F}/p_w is a normal domain representing X^w_{r,F}. Its Θ-map factors through T_w and no other weight graph.

Tangent dimensions and relative-position support. For w∈S(x_pdR), dim_E T X^w_{r,F}=n²−dn²+dn(n+1)/2+dim_E T_{x_pdR}X_w. If w_x is the relative position of the two flags, then w_x≤w is necessary for w∈S(x_pdR). Sufficiency is asserted at N=0, not for an arbitrary nonzero nilpotent N.

stages.title: The analytic trianguline variety near a generic point
stages.description:
The framed trianguline variety. Fix a residual representation r̄:G_K→GL_n(k_E) and its framed lifting space X^□_{r̄}. Let U_tri be the locus of pairs (r,δ) with δ∈T_regⁿ and D_r admitting an integral saturated triangulation of parameter δ. Define X_tri(r̄) as the reduced Zariski closure of U_tri in X^□_{r̄}×Tⁿ. Denote the full-character projection by ω′:X_tri→Tⁿ and its restriction to units by ω:X_tri→Wⁿ. The reduced structure and the closure are part of the definition.

Dimension and smooth regular triangulation locus. U_tri is open and Zariski dense in X_tri, smooth of dimension n²+dn(n+1)/2; its full-character map ω′ is smooth, as is its unit-weight map ω. X_tri is equidimensional of that dimension. These assertions concern the actual saturated regular triangulation locus, not every point of its closure.

A unique flag at generic closure points. For x=(r,δ)∈X_tri with δ∈T₀ⁿ, the localized D_r[1/t] has a unique full triangulation with parameter δ, where algebraic twists are identified after inversion of t. Its period flag is intrinsic. There is no assertion that D_r has a saturated integral triangulation with that exact tuple.

The completed analytic space imposes the localized flag. For a generic x=(r,δ), the map X̂_tri,x→X_r obtained by forgetting δ factors through the closed localized-trianguline condition X_{r,F}; both X̂_tri,x→X_{r,F} and X̂_tri,x→X_r are closed immersions, compatible with ω′ into T̂_δⁿ. The point-completion X_r is the completion of the framed lifting space at r.

Sen polynomials and infinitesimal root matching. On X_tri the τ-Sen polynomial of r equals ∏_i(T−wtτδ_i). If the residual weights are distinct, equality of these factorizations over an Artinian local algebra matches the roots by the unique permutation determined over E. Thus if wtδ=w(h) for increasing residual h, the completed Θ-map factors scheme-theoretically through T_w.

The trianguline variety local-model theorem. Let x=(r,δ)∈X_tri with δ locally algebraic generic and with distinct labelled Sen weights. Let w satisfy wtδ=w(h) for increasing h. Then X̂_tri,x≅X^w_{r,F}. Adding a D_pdR frame gives X^{pdR,w}_{r,F}→X^w_{r,F} of relative dimension dn². Forgetting the Galois frame gives X^{pdR,w}_{r,F}→X^{pdR,w}_{D,F} of relative dimension n², and the latter maps formally smoothly to X̂_{w,x_pdR} with relative dimension dn(n+1)/2. Thus R_tri[[u₁,…,u_dn²]] is noncanonically isomorphic to Ô_{X_w,x_pdR}[[v₁,…,v_{n²+dn(n+1)/2}]], with the compatible Cartan/character maps furnished by this diagram.

Normality and Cohen–Macaulayness at generic algebraic points. Under V/local-identification, X_tri is normal, locally irreducible and Cohen–Macaulay in a neighbourhood of x. The conclusion includes de Rham points and applies under the weaker locally algebraic generic, regular-Sen hypotheses of Remark 3.7.9. Smoothness requires a separate condition on the incidence component.

stages.title: Flatness, accumulation and companion geometry
stages.description:
Flatness of character and weight projections. At x satisfying V/local-identification, ω′:X_tri→Tⁿ is flat in a neighbourhood of x. Consequently its restriction-of-characters composition ω:X_tri→Wⁿ is flat there. No smoothness of either morphism is asserted.

Crystalline accumulation property. For x with algebraic unit weight, the accumulation property means that for every C>0 the set of crystalline strictly dominant noncritical points x′=(r′,δ′), with pairwise distinct Frobenius eigenvalues and ordered character weights k′_{τ,1}>⋯>k′_{τ,n} satisfying k′_{τ,i}−k′_{τ,i+1}>C, accumulates at x: there is a neighbourhood basis at x on each member of which this set is Zariski dense. The k′ are the parameter weights in decreasing order; the h used for local-model indexing are the same spectrum sorted increasingly.

Large weight gaps force saturated crystalline refinements. Let x=(r,δ)∈X_tri have algebraic dominant unit parameter weights k_{τ,i} (k_{τ,1}≥⋯≥k_{τ,n}; the source omits this hypothesis). Put e=[K:K₀] and normalize v_p(p)=1. If k_{τ,i}−k_{τ,i+1}>e·v_p((δ₁⋯δ_i)(ϖ_K)) for every τ and i<n, then the point is saturated and r is semistable. If also δ∈T_regⁿ, r is crystalline, the parameter is strictly dominant and the refinement is noncritical. This result uses the decreasing parameter-weight convention, not the increasing sorting h of the local model.

Accumulation at generic algebraic-weight points. A point x satisfying V/local-identification and having algebraic unit weight has the accumulation property of G/accumulation. This uses the crystalline density theorem on the regular triangulation locus in addition to flatness; it does not follow from flatness alone.

Tangent bounds and smoothness through Schubert geometry. For a de Rham generic regular point, dim T_x X_tri=dim X_tri−dn²+dim T_{x_pdR}X_w. With w_x the relative position and d_u=codim t^u, this is at most dim X_tri−d_{w w_x⁻¹}+ℓ(w_xw₀)+dim T_{π(x_pdR)}Ū_w−dn(n−1). Smoothness of X_tri at x is equivalent to smoothness of X_w there. It follows when Ū_w is smooth there and d_{w w_x⁻¹}=ℓ(w)−ℓ(w_x).

The refined crystalline deformation space. For strictly dominant weights k, the space of framed crystalline lifts of weight k together with an ordering of the Frobenius eigenvalues is reduced; on its smooth dense locus of generic distinct eigenvalues a Frobenius-adapted basis gives a smooth Hodge-flag map to G/B, and (r,φ)↦(r,z^kunr(φ)) is a closed immersion into X_tri sending the noncritical regular locus into U_tri.

Generic crystalline companion points. Let r be crystalline, with distinct labelled Hodge–Tate weights h and Frobenius eigenvalue ratios avoiding 1 and p^[K₀:Q_p]. Fix an ordered refinement φ and its relative position w_x. Put x_w=(r,z^{w(h)}unr(φ)) for w∈(S_n)^Σ, with the same ordered φ. Then x_w∈X_tri if and only if w_x≤w in product Bruhat order. Such algebraic changes of parameter with fixed r are the companion points in this statement.

stages.title: Local trianguline cycles and the crystalline multiplicity formula
stages.description:
Transfer of local-model cycles to Galois weight fibres. For a generic r with integral regular Sen weights, transfer the supplier’s top cycles of the Steinberg zero fibre to cycles Z_v^wt on the fixed logarithmic-weight completed fibre (equivalently, the fixed formal unit-character fibre) of Spf R_r, using the framed smooth comparison and completion cycle map. Define C_v^wt=Σ_u a_{v,u}Z_u^wt using the imported simple-module transition matrix. Their ambient codimension is dn(n+1)/2. The transfer is independent of the period frame and of algebraic twisting of the localized parameters.

Kazhdan–Lusztig identity for weight-fibre cycles. For a de Rham generic regular point with parameter permutation w and relative position w_x, [Spec Ō_{X_tri,x}^{wt}]=Σ_{w_x≤v≤w}P_{w₀w,w₀v}(1) C_v^wt as cycles on the ambient framed deformation ring. These terms are nonzero in the de Rham case. The extremal C_{w₀}^wt=Z_{w₀}^wt is nonzero exactly for de Rham r, and for crystalline r is the corresponding fixed-weight crystalline fundamental cycle.

Embedding of the fixed-character fibre. For generic δ, the fixed-full-character completed fibre X̂_tri,(r,δ)^{δ}→X_r is a closed immersion, even without locally algebraic δ. Thus its fundamental cycle can be viewed on the ambient framed Galois deformation space. This is stronger than specifying a fibre as an abstract analytic space.

The local trianguline multiplicity problem. For generic trianguline r, formulate the local multiplicity problem as existence of cycles C_{r,Π} of codimension dn(n+1)/2+n in the free abelian cycle group of Spec R_r, depending only on r and an irreducible locally analytic constituent Π, such that for every δ∈Tⁿ one has [Spec Ō_{X_tri,(r,δ)}^δ]=Σ_Π m_{δ,Π}C_{r,Π}. The left side is zero when the parameter point is absent. Here m_{δ,Π} is the finite Jordan–Hölder multiplicity in I_δ=(Ind_{B̄(K)}^{GL_n(K)}δ₁⊗δ₂ε⊗⋯⊗δ_nε^(n−1))^an. Generic r means all its triangulation parameters are in T₀ⁿ. The assertion is conjectural; existence and effectivity are proved here only in the crystalline case.

Uniqueness conditional on local cycle existence. If generic trianguline r has integral Sen weights and a family of cycles satisfying Y/multiplicity-problem exists, it is unique. This is conditional uniqueness in the free abelian cycle group; it supplies no existence statement for general r. The all-constituent triangularity input is required, including constituents induced by non-locally-algebraic parameters.

Full-character cycles and their dimensions. For de Rham generic regular r, transfer the same simple local-model cycles to C_v^δ on the full-character fibre through diagram (4.11); the additional n unramified-character coordinates are fixed. These cycles have codimension dn(n+1)/2+n, hence dimension n²−n+dn(n−1)/2, in the smooth ambient Galois ring of dimension n²+dn². The construction is independent of the auxiliary period frame.

Independence from the principal-series presentation. If two admissible presentations (w,δ) give isomorphic irreducible locally analytic constituents Π_w, the associated full-character cycles C_w^δ agree. Thus they depend only on r and Π_w in the generic de Rham setting where constructed.

Local multiplicity formula for generic crystalline representations. For crystalline r with distinct labelled Hodge–Tate weights and generic Frobenius eigenvalue ratios as in G/companion-criterion, the effective intrinsic cycles C_{r,Π} exist and satisfy Y/multiplicity-problem for every δ∈Tⁿ, including parameters absent from X_tri. Their dimension is n²−n+dn(n−1)/2. This proves the crystalline case of the local conjecture, not the general conjecture or a global locally analytic socle statement.

A rank-two split crystalline fibre calculation. For K=Q_p,n=2 and r=χ₁⊕χ₂ with χ_i=z^{h_i}unr(φ_i), h₁<h₂ and generic φ₁/φ₂, use δ=(z^{h₂}unrφ₁,z^{h₁}unrφ₂). X_tri is smooth at x, but its fixed-full-character completed fibre is reduced with two irreducible components, each of dimension 3; one is crystalline and one is not. The weight fibre has dimension 5. This is a test that flatness and smoothness of the ambient space do not imply smoothness of the character or weight projection.

stages.title: Crystabelline Hodge parameters and modification
stages.description:
Generic noncritical crystabelline Hodge parameters. Fix φ and strictly decreasing h as in the Ding setting. ΦΓ_nc(φ,h) consists of rank-n crystabelline Robba modules with D[1/t]≅⊕_i R(φ_i)[1/t], weights h and all n! Frobenius refinements noncritical. For w∈S_n the corresponding integral triangulation has successive parameters φ_{w⁻¹(i)}z^{h_i}. No étaleness is required. The permutation is common to the embeddings, whereas the BHS weight permutation lies in (S_n)^Σ.

Canonical labelled crystabelline subquotients. For each proper nonempty subset r⊂{1,…,n} of size k, construct the canonical rank-k D_r⊂D with localized Frobenius labels r and weights (h₁,…,h_k), and D^r=D/D_{rᶜ}, with labels r and weights (h_{n−k+1},…,h_n). Put D₁=D_{1,…,n−1} and C₁=D^{1,…,n−1}. The composite ι_D:D₁→D→C₁ is injective. Its source and target both have rank n−1, and their ordered weight lists differ.

Period calculation for an equal-rank torsion quotient. For an inclusion N⊂M of equal-rank Robba modules, the natural map H⁰_{φ,Γ}(M/N)→H⁰(G_K,W_dR⁺(M)/W_dR⁺(N)) is an isomorphism. If M is de Rham, this is D_dR⁺(M)/D_dR⁺(N). The cohomology is of the torsion quotient; it is not H⁰ of the localized module, where that quotient vanishes.

The rank-(n−1) injection pencil. For D∈ΦΓ_nc(φ,h), dim_E Hom(D₁,C₁)≤2. It is two exactly when n≥3 and for each i<n the quotient (D₁)^{r_i} is isomorphic to the submodule (C₁)_{r_i}, where r_i={1,…,n−1} minus {i}. In that case the quotient–isomorphism–inclusion maps α_i are pairwise linearly independent and noninjective of rank n−2. In particular n=3 always gives dimension two; the stated n=4,K=Q_p case does as well.

Recovering a Hodge extension from its injection line. The cup/pushout pairing Ext¹(R(φ_nz^{h_n}),D₁)×Hom(D₁,C₁)→Ext¹(R(φ_nz^{h_n}),C₁) has an annihilator of ι_D of dimension d and containing the nonzero extension line E[D] from 0→D₁→D→R(φ_nz^{h_n})→0. For K=Q_p this annihilator equals E[D], so (D₁,C₁,[ι_D],φ_n) determines D up to isomorphism. For general K the dimension d statement alone does not give recovery.

Refinement-compatible modified endpoint diagrams. Import the period modification D⊂D_σ from PadicHodgeTheory:P7/embedding-selective-crystalline-modification. Define D₁,σ=(D_σ)_{1,…,n−1}, C₁,σ=(D_σ)^{1,…,n−1}, and ι_{Dσ} as their inclusion–projection composite. Identify these endpoints with the modifications of D₁ and C₁ using the ambient off-σ cutoff h_{τ,n} for both. Each refinement has parameters φ_{w⁻¹(i)}z^{(T_σh)_i}; the σ-filtered endpoint maps are the original ones. The existence, uniqueness, lattice construction and D_pst comparison of D_σ are imported, not constructed again here.

The modified injection determines the σ-Hodge filtration. Every refinement of D_σ has the parameters in H/sigma-modification. The Hom-pencil bound and its rank-drop criterion hold for (D₁,σ,C₁,σ). The annihilator of ι_{Dσ} under the corresponding extension pairing is the one-dimensional line E[D_σ] for every K. Hence (D₁,σ,C₁,σ,[ι_{Dσ}],φ_n) recovers D_σ and the original σ-Hodge filtration.

A rank-three Hodge parameter recovered from an injection. For n=3 fix the Frobenius-labelled basis e₁,e₂,e₃ and a∈E minus {0,1}. At σ choose the Hodge plane span(e₁+e₂,e₁+a e₂+e₃) and Hodge line E(e₁+a e₂+e₃). The induced top lines of D₁,σ and C₁,σ are E(e₁+e₂) and E(e₁+a e₂); the projective class of their canonical injection recovers a once the labelled φ and weights are fixed. The excluded values produce a critical refinement and are not examples in ΦΓ_nc.

Every single-embedding module lifts to a regular one. The map T_σ:ΦΓ_nc(φ,h)→ΦΓ_nc(φ,T_σh) is surjective on isomorphism classes. Thus every module with the specified single varying σ-filtration comes from a module regular at every embedding, without asserting that the choice of the other filtrations is unique.

stages.title: Refinement tangent spaces and paraboline relations
stages.description:
Rank-one self-extensions as character derivatives. Use the supplier’s identification of first-order deformations with Ext¹(D,D), where ε acts on an extension by projection followed by inclusion. In rank one Ext¹(R(δ),R(δ))≅Hom_cont(K×,E), with ψ corresponding to δ(1+εψ). The smooth subspace has dimension 1, the locally σ-analytic subspace dimension 2, and the full space dimension d+1. These normalizations fix the signs of all κ-maps below.

Refinement deformation spaces and parameter derivatives. For each refinement w let Ext¹_w(D,D) be the subspace of first-order deformations lifting its integral triangulation. Define κ_w:Ext¹_w→Hom_cont((K×)^n,E) from the derivatives of its n lifted characters, in their ordered graded positions. Ext¹_g(D,D) denotes the de Rham first-order subspace. The underlying deformation functors and their representing rings are imported; this target specifies their simultaneous refinement subspaces and derivatives.

Dimensions and Weyl transport of refinement tangents. The dimensions are dim Ext¹(D,D)=1+n²d, dim Ext¹_g=1+n(n−1)d/2, and dim Ext¹_w=1+n(n+1)d/2. Each κ_w is surjective and κ_w⁻¹(Hom_sm(T(K),E))=Ext¹_g. On Ext¹_g, κ_{w₂}=(w₂w₁⁻¹)κ_{w₁}, with the permutation action matching the ordered character positions.

The common zero-parameter quotient. Let Ext¹₀(D,D)=ker κ_w; it is independent of w, lies in Ext¹_g and has dimension 1−n+dn(n−1)/2. Put barExt¹=Ext¹/Ext¹₀ and similarly for subspaces containing Ext¹₀. Then barExt¹_w≅Hom_cont(T(K),E), barExt¹_g≅Hom_sm(T(K),E), and dim barExt¹=dn(n+1)/2+n. This full-kernel identity applies to the regular original D and must not be transferred unchanged to D_σ.

De Rham deformation directions up to scalar twist. Define Ext¹_{g′}(D,D) as de Rham deformations up to a rank-one character twist. Let Hom_{g′}(T(K),E)=Hom_sm(T(K),E)+{ψ∘det:ψ∈Hom_cont(K×,E)}. Then Ext¹_{g′}=κ_w⁻¹(Hom_{g′}) for every w and has dimension 1+d(n(n−1)/2+1). Weyl transport of κ holds on this larger subspace.

Paraboline deformation subspaces. For a standard parabolic P with ordered block sizes n₁,…,n_r summing to n and a saturated P-filtration F_P of D, let M_i=gr_i F_P have rank n_i. Ext¹_{F_P}(D,D) consists of deformations lifting F_P, and κ_{F_P} sends them to the tuple in ∏_i Ext¹(M_i,M_i). A refinement w is compatible when its full flag refines F_P. Define quotient versions only after proving Ext¹₀⊂Ext¹_{F_P}.

Paraboline dimensions and quotient product formulas. κ_{F_P} is surjective and dim Ext¹_{F_P}=1+d dim P, where dim P=Σ_{i≤j}n_i n_j. For a compatible refinement w, Ext¹_w is the inverse image of ∏Ext¹_{w_i}(M_i,M_i). The quotient barExt¹_{F_P}≅∏barExt¹(M_i,M_i) has dimension d dim(B∩L_P)+n, and its compatible trianguline quotients identify with the product of graded trianguline quotients. The sign before n is positive.

Blockwise de Rham directions and Weyl transport. Let Ext¹_{F_P,g′} be the κ_{F_P}-inverse image of ∏Ext¹_{g′}(M_i,M_i). Its compatible-refinement derivative image is Hom_{P,g′}=Hom_sm(T(K),E)+Σ_i{ψ_i∘det_i}, of dimension n+rd. Derivative transport is equivariant for W_P, and membership is equivalent to the displayed blockwise condition.

stages.title: Partial de Rham deformation spaces
stages.description:
Partial de Rham self-extension conditions. For J⊂Σ a Robba module is J-de Rham when dim_E D_dR,τ equals its rank for every τ∈J. Write Ext¹_σ(D,D) for self-extensions that are (Σ minus {σ})-de Rham, and intersect this subspace with the refinement, paraboline and g′ conditions to obtain Ext¹_{σ,?}. Quotients barExt¹_{σ,?} are taken by Ext¹₀ whenever it is contained. For a de Rham rank-one character, Ext¹_σ≅Hom_σ(K×,E).

Partial de Rham dimensions and paraboline products. For regular D, dim Ext¹_σ(D,D)=1+(d−1)n(n−1)/2+n². For a P-filtration, dim Ext¹_{σ,F_P}=1+(d−1)n(n−1)/2+dim P; its graded map is surjective and induces barExt¹_{σ,F_P}≅∏_i barExt¹_σ(M_i,M_i). Compatible refinement quotients identify with the product of graded refinement quotients, and κ_w induces barExt¹_{σ,w}≅Hom_σ(T(K),E).

Tangent dimensions for the modified module. For D_σ, dim Ext¹=1+n²d, dim Ext¹_g=1+n(n−1)/2, and dim Ext¹_{F_P}=1+d dim P. Every de Rham deformation lifts every such P-filtration, and the graded paraboline map is surjective. However κ_w⁻¹(Hom_sm) has dimension 1+dn(n−1)/2, so strictly contains Ext¹_g when d>1. The partial dimensions are dim Ext¹_σ=1+n² and dim Ext¹_{σ,F_P}=1+dim P.

Modification of first-order deformations. For each deformation D̃ over R_{K,E[ε]/ε²}, construct a unique D̃_σ⊃D̃ with the same localization, the same σ-Sen weights, and τ≠σ Sen weights, as E-weights, all equal to h_{τ,n}. It reduces to D_σ and defines an E-linear map T_σ:Ext¹(D,D)→Ext¹(D_σ,D_σ), preserving partial de Rhamness and saturated filtrations. Constant E-weights do not impose vanishing of nilpotent Sen operators.

Kernel and restricted surjectivity of modification. ker T_σ has dimension (d−1)n(n−1)/2 and lies in Ext¹_g(D,D). Restrictions to Ext¹_g, Ext¹_σ and Ext¹_{σ,F_P} are surjective onto the corresponding spaces for D_σ, with this same kernel. The graded diagram commutes, and Ext¹_{σ,F_P}(D_σ,D_σ)→∏Ext¹_σ(M_i,σ,M_i,σ) is surjective. The full map on Ext¹ is not surjective when d>1 and n≥2.

The modified de Rham zero-parameter quotient. Define Ext¹₀(D_σ,D_σ) as the kernel of κ_w restricted to Ext¹_g(D_σ,D_σ). It is independent of w, has dimension 1−n+n(n−1)/2, and is strictly smaller than ker κ_w on the full refinement space if d>1. Define modified barExt¹ by this de Rham kernel. The maps κ_w:Ext¹_g→Hom_sm are surjective and obey Weyl transport.

Modification induces partial tangent quotient isomorphisms. Ext¹₀(D,D)=T_σ⁻¹(Ext¹₀(D_σ,D_σ)), and T_σ maps these zero subspaces surjectively. For *=g,σ or (σ,F_P), it induces barExt¹_*(D,D)≅barExt¹_*(D_σ,D_σ). The paraboline product isomorphisms commute with this comparison and the graded modifications.

stages.title: Higher intertwining and recovery of Hodge parameters
stages.description:
Pullback and pushout along a Hodge injection. For ι:D₁→C₁ define ι⁻:Ext¹(C₁,D₁)→Ext¹(D₁,D₁) by pullback and ι⁺:Ext¹(C₁,D₁)→Ext¹(C₁,C₁) by pushout. Write Ext¹_ι for their respective image subspaces. Both maps are E-linear and preserve de Rham local conditions. This notation includes noninjective ι, but later rigidity theorems specify injectivity.

Dimensions of the exceptional noninjective images. Assume dim Hom(D₁,C₁)=2 and use the rank-(n−2) maps α_i. Each Ext¹_{α_i} has dimension (n−1)(n−2)d. For distinct i,j their intersection has dimension (n−1)(n−3)d+d−1 and their sum has dimension 1+n(n−2)d. Both assertions hold on the D₁ and on the C₁ side.

Self-extension images determine the injection line. If ι:D₁→C₁ is injective, both Ext¹_ι image spaces have dimension 1+(n−1)(n−2)d and contain the relevant de Rham self-Ext space. For any ι′, equality of either image with the corresponding image of ι is equivalent to ι′=aι for a∈E×. For a de Rham M∈Ext¹(C₁,D₁), the smooth derivatives κ_{φ₁}(ι⁻M) and κ_{φ₁}(ι⁺M) agree.

The signed matched-extension relation. Define I_ι as the image of M↦(ι⁻M,−ι⁺M) in Ext¹(D₁,D₁)×Ext¹(C₁,C₁). Equivalently its points are pairs arising from one common extension with the indicated minus sign. For native linear maps f:U→V and g:U→W this is LinearMap.range(f.prod(−g)); it is a submodule, not the product of the two separate ranges.

The matched relation determines the Hodge injection. For injective ι and ι′, I_ι=I_{ι′} if and only if ι′∈E×ι. For D,D′ in the nonempty family ΦΓ_nc(D₁,C₁,φ_n) with the same fixed endpoints, equality I_D=I_{D′} is equivalent to equality of the injection lines; when K=Q_p it is equivalent to D≅D′.

The first/last-filtration higher-intertwining criterion. Let F be D₁⊂D and G be R(φ_nz^{h₁})⊂D. For D̃∈Ext¹_F(D,D), write κ_F(D̃)=(D̃₁,ψ). Then D̃ also belongs to Ext¹_G if and only if D̃₁⊗R(1−εψ) belongs to Ext¹_{ι_D}(D₁,D₁). In that case κ_{G,2}=ψ and there is M∈Ext¹(C₁,D₁) with D̃₁=ι_D⁻M⊗R(1+εψ) and κ_{G,1}=ι_D⁺M⊗R(1+εψ). All Robba coefficients are over K.

Two paraboline spaces span self-Ext. dim(Ext¹_F∩Ext¹_G)=1+(n²−2n+2)d, and Ext¹_F+Ext¹_G=Ext¹(D,D). Here each of Ext¹_F and Ext¹_G has dimension 1+(n²−n+1)d. Compute dim(F+G)=dim F+dim G−dim(F∩G), subtracting the whole intersection dimension including its constant term.

All noncritical refinements span the tangent space. The sum map ⊕_{w∈S_n}Ext¹_w(D,D)→Ext¹(D,D) is surjective, and remains surjective after quotienting by Ext¹₀. This is proved by rank induction from the first/last-filtration spanning theorem and the graded refinement preimage formula, rather than using this result as its own prerequisite.

The higher-intertwining relation on tangent quotients. Set V=(barExt¹(D₁,D₁)×Hom(K×,E))⊕(barExt¹(C₁,C₁)×Hom(K×,E)). Define L(D,D₁,C₁) to consist of ((a,ψ),(b,−ψ)) for which representatives ã,b̃ satisfy (ã⊗R(1−εψ), b̃⊗R(1+εψ))∈I_D. Existence of such representatives is required; an unqualified condition on arbitrary representatives before quotienting is insufficient.

A tangent presentation that recovers the Hodge parameter. There is a natural short exact sequence 0→L(D,D₁,C₁)→V→barExt¹(D,D)→0, where the last map adds the two paraboline classes. For fixed endpoints and φ_n, L(D,D₁,C₁)=L(D′,D₁,C₁) if and only if ι_D′∈E×ι_D; for K=Q_p this is equivalent to D≅D′.

Partial extension images recover the modified injection. For injective ι_σ:D₁,σ→C₁,σ, use Ext¹_σ(C₁,σ,D₁,σ) in the pullback and pushout maps. Their image dimensions are 1+(n−1)(n−2), they contain the respective de Rham self-Ext spaces, and equality of either image determines ι_σ up to E×. The signed relation I_{Dσ} determines D_σ up to isomorphism for every K.

Higher intertwining with one varying Hodge embedding. For D̃_σ∈Ext¹_{σ,F}(D_σ,D_σ) with κ_F=(D̃₁,σ,ψ), ψ∈Hom_σ(K×,E), the additional G-filtration exists exactly when D̃₁,σ⊗R_{K,E[ε]/ε²}(1−εψ) belongs to the partial injection image. In this case κ_{G,2}=ψ and a common M∈Ext¹_σ(C₁,σ,D₁,σ) gives both graded deformations with the same +εψ twist, as in I/higher-intertwining.

The single-embedding higher-intertwining relation. Set V_σ=(barExt¹_σ(D₁,σ,D₁,σ)×Hom_σ(K×,E))⊕(barExt¹_σ(C₁,σ,C₁,σ)×Hom_σ(K×,E)), using the modified de Rham zero subspaces. Define L_σ(D_σ,D₁,σ,C₁,σ) by the signed opposite-twist representative condition with I_{Dσ}, exactly as in I/higher-relation. Both the C₁,σ endpoint and the σ-subscript on the partial condition are essential.

The single-embedding recovery exact sequence. There is a short exact sequence 0→L_σ(D_σ,D₁,σ,C₁,σ)→V_σ→barExt¹_σ(D_σ,D_σ)→0. For fixed endpoints and φ_n, equality of these L_σ relations is equivalent to D_σ≅D′_σ, for every finite K/Q_p. Hence the relation determines the original σ-Hodge filtration.

Modification identifies the two recovery sequences. Let V(D₁,C₁)_σ be the partial subspace of V and L(D,D₁,C₁)_σ=L∩V_σ. Modification T_σ identifies its exact sequence 0→L_σ→V_σ→barExt¹_σ(D,D)→0 with the modified sequence of I/sigma-recovery-exact, by isomorphisms on all three terms. Thus the original module’s partial tangent relation recovers its σ-Hodge filtration.

Partial refinement spaces generate all partial deformations. For both D and D_σ the map ⊕_{w∈S_n}Ext¹_{σ,w}→Ext¹_σ is surjective, as is its barExt quotient. This generation statement includes the original and modified modules with their different zero kernels.

stages.title: Ordered-regular local deformation applications
stages.description:
Ordered-regular parameters and ordinary flags. Define NT-regularity of δ=(δ₁,…,δ_n) by δ_i/δ_j≠∏ττ^aτ for every i<j and every aτ≥0. A parameter is ordinary when each δ_i(ϖ_K) is a p-adic unit. For an ordinary tuple, a Galois representation is trianguline of that parameter exactly when it has a G_K-stable flag whose graded characters are δ_i∘Art_K⁻¹. These conditions are ordered and use the arithmetic reciprocity normalization of NT.

Strictness and uniqueness for ordered-regular parameters. If ρ has an integral triangulation of NT-regular parameter δ, it is unique and strict: for 0≤i≤n−1 the H⁰ of (D_rig(ρ)/Fil_i)(δ_{i+1}⁻¹) is one-dimensional. There is no δ_{n+1} condition. This theorem needs no cyclotomic exceptional-ratio exclusion.

The ordered-regular deformation condition and weight tangent. Given (ρ,F,δ) with δ NT-regular, let D_{ρ,F,δ}(A) be triples (ρ_A,F_A,δ_A) reducing to them, modulo conjugation by 1+M_n(m_A) transporting the flag; F_A is an integral saturated triangulation of D_rig(ρ_A). Its tangent identifies with H¹_tri,δ(K,adρ)⊂H¹(K,adρ). Restrict δ_A to (O_K×)^n to obtain the weight map to Ŵ_{δ|units}; its derivative is the weight-tangent map.

Representability under the weaker ordered regularity condition. For NT-regular δ the forgetful transformation D_{ρ,F,δ}→D_ρ is relatively representable and injective on A-points for every A∈Art_E. If ρ is absolutely irreducible, both unframed functors are prorepresentable and R_ρ→R_{ρ,F,δ} is surjective. Absolute irreducibility is required for this unframed prorepresentability claim.

Fixed-weight noncritical tangent directions are de Rham. Suppose ρ is de Rham, trianguline of NT-regular δ, and wt_NT,τδ₁<⋯<wt_NT,τδ_n are integers for every τ. The kernel of H¹_tri,δ(K,adρ)→T_{δ|units}W lies in H¹_g(K,adρ)=ker(H¹(K,adρ)→H¹(K,adρ⊗B_dR)). Equivalently every first-order trianguline lift with fixed unit characters is de Rham. The inclusion is not asserted to be equality.

Numerically noncritical character tuples. Let k_{τ,i}=wt_NT,τδ_i be strictly increasing integers. Call δ numerically noncritical if, for every τ and 1≤i<n, v_p((δ₁⋯δ_i)(p))<k_{τ,i+1}−k_{τ,i}, with v_p(p)=1 and p the rational prime viewed in K×. A native arithmetic adapter records these inequalities for rational prefix slopes s_i and integral weights k; it is not itself a definition of a Robba character or of its valuation.

A Weil–Deligne valuation criterion for noncritical triangulations. Let ρ be de Rham with distinct ascending labelled weights k and a full WD(ρ)-stable flag with rank-one graded characters χ₁,…,χ_n. For every τ require v_p(χ₁(p))<k_{τ,2}+Σ_{τ′≠τ}k_{τ′,1}; for 2≤i<n require v_p((χ₁⋯χ_i)(p))<k_{τ,i+1}+Σ_{τ′≠τ}k_{τ′,i}+Σ_{τ′}Σ_{j<i}k_{τ′,j}. Then ρ has the noncritical triangulation δ_i=(χ_i∘Art_K)∏ττ^(−k_{τ,i}). Equivalently the numerical noncriticality of this δ suffices. A WD flag and de Rhamness are hypotheses, not conclusions of numerical inequalities alone.

Three rank-two de Rham triangulation cases. For K=Q_p, a rank-two de Rham ρ with k₁<k₂ and distinct WD semisimple characters χ₁,χ₂ has: if N≠0, exactly one triangulation, noncritical, after ordering χ₁=χ₂|·|; if potentially crystalline and irreducible or reducible indecomposable, exactly two, both noncritical, with the two χ-orderings and the same k-ordering; if split ψ₁⊕ψ₂ with wtψ_i=k_i, exactly two, one with ordered k and one critical with reversed graded weights. No two-refinement assertion is made when χ₁=χ₂.

A local tangent constraint on a regular trianguline closure. Let ρ be absolutely irreducible with NT-regular δ, and work in a neighbourhood U_v of its pseudorepresentation carrying a universal representation. In U_v×T_NT,reg let V_tri be the pointwise trianguline locus and Z_v its reduced Zariski closure. V_tri is Zariski open in Z_v. At (ρ,δ)∈V_tri the projection T Z_v→H¹(K,adρ) is injective with image contained in H¹_tri,δ; its character coordinate is forced by the unique triangulation. This is not a claimed isomorphism with the whole trianguline tangent space.

From Zariski-dense interpolation to the KPX density hypothesis. In the setting of N/closure-tangent, a merely Zariski-dense set X_alg of trianguline points can be enlarged to a set satisfying the KPX admissible-cover density requirement. On each connected normal reduced component, choose a Zariski-open dense U′ where the relevant coherent Herr H⁰ sheaves and their t_τ quotients are locally free and the rank-one section is nonzero and saturated. Then X_alg∪U′ is dense for the required admissible cover. Normalization, connectedness and the sheaf base-change conditions are retained.

A nontrianguline rank-two module has no (φ,Γ)-stable finite-dimensional subspace. For K=Q_p and an absolutely irreducible two-dimensional E-representation V that is nontrianguline even after finite coefficient extension, D_rig(V) contains no nonzero finite-dimensional E-subspace stable under φ and Γ, also after a finite coefficient extension. Such a subspace would contain a common eigenvector of φ and Γ, which generates a rank-one (φ,Γ)-submodule whose saturation is a triangulation.

The nontrianguline polynomial-connection kernel argument. Under N/rank-two-nontrianguline, suppose the differential-equation supplier gives finite-dimensionality of ker P(∇)⊂D_rig(V) for every nonzero P∈E[X]. Then P(∇) is injective: ∇ commutes with φ and Γ, so its kernel is a finite-dimensional subspace stable under φ and Γ, which vanishes by the preceding theorem. The finiteness theorem and the connection itself remain owned by the differential-equation and period suppliers.
